{'result': '# New hire handbook

**Document type**: initialization
**Role**: Handbook issued when you join the product R&D organisation
**Audience**: New hires

Welcome to the product engineering group. Before your career clock starts, this handbook sets out the public rules. Everything in it is part of the published game design, and you can use it for long-term planning.

## What is published

- **Published**: This handbook covers the published rules: the level ladder, visible stats, quarterly energy and main actions, the timeline and promotion windows, performance grades, risk and failure rules, and monthly pay.
- **Not published**: Not listed here. You can only infer these from emails, meeting notes, manager feedback and outcomes: promotion score thresholds, talk tiers, performance formula weights, hidden risk and random event odds.
- **Note**: You cannot see everything that is happening in the organisation. Plan across quarters and years with incomplete information.

## Levels

There are ten levels, L1 to L10. Higher levels expect broader impact and set a higher bar for promotion.

A promotion window opens every 6 months. The bar depends on Skill, Network, Output and level; the exact thresholds are hidden.

| Level | Name | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | Junior engineer | Carries out tasks with clear guidance |
| L2 | Engineer | Owns modules independently |
| L3 | Senior engineer | Owns core modules, with growing technical responsibility |
| L4 | Staff engineer | Works on critical systems with major project impact |
| L5 | Principal / team lead | Leads a subsystem or small team |
| L6 | Senior principal / tech lead | Leads large programmes or sets technical direction |
| L7 | Director of engineering | Department-level technical strategy |
| L8 | Senior director | Cross-department technical planning |
| L9 | Distinguished fellow / architecture committee | Company-wide technical influence |
| L10 | Chief architect / fellow | Makes company-wide technical decisions over a long horizon |

## Visible statistics

Shown on your panel or in the monthly summary. These are your main inputs for decisions.

| Key | Name | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Health | Health | 0–10 | Physical and mental stamina. Long-term overwork wears it down |
| Dignity | Dignity | 0–10 | Self-respect and recognition at work. Staying low for too long triggers a crisis |
| Skill | Skill | 0–unbounded | Professional capability |
| Network | Network | 0–unbounded | The working relationships you can draw on |
| Level | Level | L1–L10 | Current career level |
| Output | Output | 0–unbounded | The visible results you have built up over time |
| Wealth | Wealth | unbounded | Cumulative wealth |
| Energy | Energy | 0–3 | Your energy budget for the quarter, spent on quarterly actions |
| CurrentLevelDuration | Months at current level | 0–unbounded | Consecutive months at present level |

## Time

- Length: 48 months
- Story events per month: 3
- Each month:
  - 1. A new month starts and you are paid the base salary for your level
  - 2. Up to 3 story events are drawn from the pool
  - 3. You play through the story events and make your choices
  - 4. At the end of a quarter (months 3, 6, 9…), once the month’s event quota is full, you move on to quarterly energy actions
  - 5. Allocate your 3 Energy points for the quarter. You can pick the same action more than once, until you finish or skip
  - 6. Choose one quarterly main action (or none)
  - 7. Your stats are settled. Crossing a red line may bring a written or verbal warning
  - 8. Every half year: a 1:1 with your manager (no decision needed)
  - 9. Every 6 months: formal performance review and bonus

## Energy actions

3 Energy per quarter. Unused Energy does not roll over.

- Energy each quarter: 3
- Unused Energy carries over: no

| Action | Energy cost | Stat change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| High-intensity work | 2 | Output +, Health -, Dignity - |
| Skill learning | 2 | Skill +, Health - |
| Network maintenance | 1 | Network +, Dignity + |
| Defuse legacy risk | 2 | None (or an effect you cannot see) |
| Mental recovery | 1 | Dignity + |
| Health recovery | 1 | Health + |
| Prepare report materials | 1 | Output +, Dignity + |

## Main actions

Each quarter, pick one main action or none.

- Most you can pick each quarter: 1
- You may take no main action: yes

| Action | Stat change |
| --- | --- |
| Apply for a key project | Output +, Skill +, Network + |
| Report results to your manager | Output +, Network +, Dignity + |
| Fight for resources | Output +, Network + |
| Apply for rotation | Skill +, Network + |
| Showcase results | Output +, Dignity + |
| Build a mentorship | Skill +, Network + |
| Repair a key relationship | Network +, Dignity + |
| Lay low and reduce risk | Health + |

## Wealth and monthly pay

You are paid a base salary each month according to your level: 0.3 Wealth a month at L1, rising with each level to 9.1 a month at L10.

| Level | Monthly base (Wealth) |
| --- | --- |
| L1 | 0.3 |
| L2 | 0.4 |
| L3 | 0.5 |
| L4 | 0.7 |
| L5 | 1.0 |
| L6 | 1.5 |
| L7 | 2.3 |
| L8 | 3.6 |
| L9 | 5.7 |
| L10 | 9.1 |

## Performance review

- How often: Formal review every 6 months
- Note: Performance combines Skill, Network, Output, level, etc.; bonus is a multiple of base monthly pay. The bands are published in advance and applied the same way to everyone.

| Grade | Meaning | Bonus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S | Exceptional | base monthly ×3 |
| A | Strong | base monthly ×2 |
| B | Solid | base monthly ×1 |
| C | Weak | base monthly ×0.25 |
| D | Very weak | no bonus |

## Risk and failure

The red lines are not in the onboarding slides. Old hands will tell you what tends to blow up. The timing and counts you learn by playing.

### What people say

- Old landmines all go off at once, and half a year of work vanishes!
- In a review your teammates use jargon you cannot keep up with. You nod and promise to look into it…

### Ways people say a run ends

- Blackout — your body gives out before the KPIs do. Game over
- Breakdown — after months with no dignity left, you send a resignation email
- Trust crisis — after a second blow-up, the company says you have used up its trust
- Dismissed for capability — two weak half-year reviews and you hand the badge in
- Isolated — work that needs other people cannot get done, and you resign
- Broke — months with an empty wallet
- Obsolete — your manager suggests a role that matches what you can actually do

Survive all 48 months and you may earn a career summary worth showing.'}

# Event decision

Use this Skill when `observe` shows a story event with choices. Use the status and priority from `career-state-assessment`.

## Steps

1. **Read each option.** For each one, estimate in a few words its likely effect on Health, Dignity, Skill, Network, Output and Wealth. Use the wording of the option and the published effect directions. Do not assume exact numbers.
2. **Look for delayed costs.** Mark any option that gains now but may create later trouble, for example overwork, damaging a relationship, cutting corners, or taking on risk. Risks may settle months later.
3. **Score against the priority.**
   - `recover`: prefer options that protect or restore Health, even if growth is slower.
   - `protect`: prefer options that protect Dignity and avoid losing Wealth.
   - `reduce-risk`: prefer cautious options and avoid anything with a likely delayed cost.
   - `prepare-review`: prefer options that produce visible Output or results, as long as they do not seriously harm Health or Dignity.
   - `grow-balanced`: prefer options that build the lagging growth statistic, with a modest cost at most.
4. **Choose.** Pick the option that best serves the priority with the least delayed risk. If two options are close, choose the safer one.

## Rules

- Never trade a large loss in Health or Dignity for a small gain elsewhere.
- When Health and Dignity are both near the top of their range, a small cost to one of them is acceptable for a clear gain in Output, Skill or Network. Keeping them at the maximum earns nothing extra.
- Do not try to guess hidden formulas or follow event-specific scripts. Reason from the option text, the current state and the feedback received.
- Treat repeated small harms as serious, because they accumulate.

## Action

Call `take_action` with the chosen option. In `notes`, write one short sentence giving the main reason, for example: "Protect Health; it has fallen for two quarters."

description: Reads the current game state and recent feedback and produces a short status with one top priority. Use before every decision in the Career Survival game.

# Career state assessment

Use this Skill before every story event and every quarterly phase. Its output is a short status that the other Skills use to choose an action. Keep it brief.

## Inputs

- The latest `observe` result: statistics, month, current event or phase, available choices.
- Any warnings or feedback returned by the last `take_action`.
- `check_latest_logs` only when the last few decisions are unclear or a warning appeared. Do not call it every turn.
- The public handbook, read once at the start of the game.

## What to assess

1. **Survival statistics.** For Health and Dignity (range 0 to 10), judge whether each is comfortable, getting low, or low, relative to its range. Note whether it rose or fell over recent months. For Wealth, note whether it is positive and whether it is trending down.
2. **Growth statistics.** Compare Skill, Network and Output with each other. Note any that are clearly lagging, because promotion depends on all three together.
3. **Warnings.** Any warning about overwork, standing or accumulating risk is important evidence, even if the visible numbers still look acceptable. Read the narrative lines in the `events` text as well as the numbers: remarks from colleagues, HR or the manager often signal rising hidden risk or weak standing before any statistic moves. Note whether the same kind of warning has repeated over recent months.
4. **Timing.** Work out the month within the quarter, whether the quarterly phase is next, and how many months remain until the next six-month review and promotion window. Note CurrentLevelDuration.
5. **Recent outcomes.** Note the last review grade, what the manager's feedback asked for, and whether the last promotion window succeeded. A middling grade with feedback asking for clearer results means visible Output is behind, even if other statistics are growing.
6. **Buffer.** If Health and Dignity are both near the top of their range, that is spare buffer, not a goal in itself. Unused buffer earns nothing until the end of the run, so it can be spent on growth.

## Output

Write a short status in this form:

- Risks: which statistics are at risk, and why, in one line.
- Lagging: which growth statistic is behind, if any.
- Timing: months to the next review, and whether this is a review-preparation period.
- Priority: exactly one of `recover`, `protect`, `prepare-review`, `grow-balanced`, `reduce-risk`.

## Choosing the priority

- `recover`: Health is low or falling over several months, or a warning about overwork appeared.
- `protect`: Dignity is low or falling, or Wealth is becoming negative.
- `reduce-risk`: warnings suggest hidden risk is building, even if visible statistics are fine. A risk warning that repeats, or that sounds more serious than the last one, always qualifies.
- `prepare-review`: survival statistics are safe and either a review is close, or the last review was middling and the feedback asked for clearer results.
- `grow-balanced`: everything is safe and no review is close.

If more than one applies, choose the first one in this list. Survival comes before growth.

In the last few months of the run, lean toward ending with Health and Dignity comfortable, because the final state counts.
